html:
The Arauco War was the long conflict between the Mapuche people and the Spanish in southern Chile, from the 1550s into the 1800s. The Mapuche kept their independence south of the Biobío River.

In 1553 Mapuche warriors led by Lautaro, a former groom of the conquistador, killed Pedro de Valdivia at Tucapel. In 1598 a great rising after the battle of Curalaba destroyed all seven Spanish towns south of the Biobío. Spain then accepted the river as a frontier, guarded by forts and paid soldiers, the only standing army of its kind in the Americas.

War alternated with parleys, called parlamentos, in which the Spanish treated the Mapuche almost as a foreign nation. The poem La Araucana by Alonso de Ercilla made the Mapuche famous in Spain. Their freedom ended only with the occupation of Araucanía by Chile in the 1880s.
